title: Make tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 derive the parity counts instead of hard-coding them
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: observed: RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-001 exited 1 on a tree where rules-parity says 'AGREE 12 facts <- 16 twinned entries, 28 patterns; 47 settled entries not compared'. C-001 printed FAIL for the pinned 'AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 48 settled…' string, and its -ExpectFacts 11 run failed wi…
RuleCases.ps1 no longer hard-codes the 'AGREE N facts <- M twinned entries, P patterns' counts (about six places plus the C-005 fixture): partial
A slice that declares one more twinned rule leaves the rule-copy cases green (C-001 exits 0 on that tree): missing

Should tests/rules/SettledCountProbe.ps1:125 (the stub tool's literal AGREE line) be derived from the recount in this slice, or left as a follow-up? It is outside the slice's named file. Left as-is, the Misclassified probe still turns red on a read-back regression, but after the next twinned slice it can no longer tell a real misclassification from a stale stub line.
Count-free case titles versus titles computed from the recount (the proposal chose count-free; computed titles need the counts to exist before the cases are declared).
A separate Format-AgreeLine function versus inline string interpolation at each site (one spelling chosen, at the price of a function to keep in step with the parity tool's wording).

The recount in RuleCases.ps1 versus a shared tests/rules/RuleCounts.ps1 that SettledCountProbe.ps1 could also use. The in-file placement was chosen because of the scratch-copy risk, but a shared file would make the SettledCountProbe.ps1:125 follow-up cheaper.
One literal-count guard rule with five regexes versus a second rule against reading counts back (rejected: read-back has too many spellings for a regex to catch).

Loop shape: attempts 3 to 7 were each taken back as STALE because uat moved under the slice before its merge out (SL-070, SL-071, SL-072, SL-073), and none of those merges touched SL-069's files. Every lap re-runs about 10 minutes of engine-backed checks to confirm an overlap that is empty. If the merge step checked file overlap first, or merged out immediately after the uat-in merge, the lap would not recur.

Still open from attempts 5 and 6, and not built: C-007 compares import-rule names as quoted text in the harness's human-readable NOT RUN line. A machine-readable `harness: not-run-json` line, compared as a parsed list, would close that class of mismatch. It is for a person to rank.
